hypothesis: Under the sparse-mixing / independent-mechanism-analysis (IMA) inductive-bias class (Z with independent non-Gaussian marginals; A drawn as Haar orthogonal masked by Bernoulli(s) and re-orthonormalised, for s in {0.5, 0.25}), sklearn FastICA achieves Amari index <= 0.02 at N = 10000 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8} and every sparsity level; sparser (s=0.25) recovery is at least as good as denser (s=0.5) modulo a 0.01 tolerance at every d_Z; the smallest N reaching Amari <= 0.03 grows polynomially in d_Z (fitted log-log slope b <= 3.0) for both sparsities; and the Amari(N) curve at each (d_Z, s) is nonincreasing modulo 0.01. This is the sparse-mixing/IMA sibling of instrument 8 (linear-ICA) --- a second partial positive resolution of SIC-C-c.

controls.description: All randomness derives from BASE_SEED = 0 via numpy SeedSequence keyed by (BASE_SEED, d_Z, trial, int(round(s*1000))); sklearn FastICA random_state = trial. Running twice yields identical Amari values at every grid point.
Within each (d_Z, trial, sparsity) triple, one (A, Z_full) is drawn at max(N_VALUES) and every smaller N re-uses the first N samples as a prefix, so the sample-complexity curve varies only in N.
Amari is averaged over TRIALS = 8 independent (A, Z) draws per grid point; finite-sample FastICA variance is smoothed enough that monotonicity holds within a 0.01 tolerance.
The Amari index is verified in the unit tests to be exactly 0 on the identity matrix and on any signed permutation matrix (the ICA identifiability class), and > 0.5 on the all-ones mixture.
The mask retry / keep-diagonal fallback path is tallied per (d_Z, sparsity) cell and emitted in the summary under 'scheme_counts', so any grid point that relied on the milder fallback is auditable.

gates.criterion: Averaged Amari at N = 10000 is <= 0.02 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8} and every sparsity in {0.5, 0.25}.
At N = 10000, amari(s=0.25) - amari(s=0.5) <= 0.01 for every d_Z (sparser recovery is at least as good as denser modulo the 0.01 finite-sample tolerance).
For every sparsity and every d_Z there is a smallest N reaching averaged Amari <= 0.03; the fitted log-log slope b of log(N_needed) = a + b log(d_Z) is <= 3.0 for both sparsities.
For every (d_Z, sparsity), the averaged Amari curve is nonincreasing in N modulo a numerical tolerance of 0.01.
